title: define statement: unsettled interactions (static/no-clause vars, internal and program routines, double initial values)
description: Found reviewing domain-pascal-hsb.  The reference (7.2 p. 7-3, 7.2.2 p. 7-5, 7.2.3 p. 7-6, 7.3.2 p. 7-8, 7.3.4 p. 7-11) does not settle these; current behaviour is inconsistent or silent.  (1) define x of a 'static' or clause-less unit var: define AFTER the var makes it global (define_item rewrites Static{global:true}); define BEFORE the var (Method 3 order) leaves it local - only an 'extern' var is converted (check.rs var_decl pre_defined).  Static says 'keep its name local'.  (2) define of an 'internal' routine: silently accepted, routine stays local.  (3) define of a routine in a PROGRAM: 7.3.2 'A routine name from the main program can never become a global symbol'; silently accepted, stays local.  (4) Two initial values: 'define a := 1; a := 2;' or 'var a: extern integer := 3; define a := 4;' - the last silently wins (7.2.2.1 p. 7-5 says data with an extern declaration is ignored until the variable is defined).  Candidate owner questions; do not change behaviour without a ruling.
